title: Compatibility Sentinel: orchestrated escape paths for pinned model versions
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Define and implement a tolerant, auditable fallback orchestration layer — the Compatibility Sentinel — that enforces safe escape paths for requests pinned to specific model versions. This ticket covers policy language, runtime decision order, deprecation signals, observability hooks, and a canary rollout plan. Goals: ensure pinned routes remain available or degrade gracefully with predictable performance and documented audit trails; avoid silent semantic regressions when automatic substitutions occur.
acceptance_criteria: Define a declarative fallback policy schema that can be attached to any pinned model route (YAML/JSON).
Runtime implements deterministic decision steps for pinned requests: same-region-compatible-variant -> regional-downgrade -> cross-region-redirect -> hold-and-queue -> failure-with-explanation.
Deprecation flow: automated soft-warning (30 days), enforced replacement window, and opt-in auto-substitution with explicit audit entries.
End-to-end tests for policy permutations (latency-first, cost-first, strict-compat) pass in CI with >=95% coverage for decision branches.
Console shows per-pin audit trail (who/pin/version/timestamp/replacement-path) and per-route fallback metrics in the runtime-1.34 release dashboard.
Security review completed and KMS-backed audit log fields approved.
implementation_notes: Design a compact policy model: priority list of fallback candidates, max allowed latency delta, semantic compatibility flag, and deprecation windows.
Policy attaches to model_pin object stored in config DB. Runtime evaluates policy atomically per request with a bounded decision timeout (recommendation: 50ms for decision logic).
Introduce a 'replacement_reason' enum in logs: {DEPRECATION, CAPACITY, INCOMPATIBLE, COST_OPTIMIZATION, REGION_OUTAGE}.
Implement a dry-run mode: log simulated substitution but do not change runtime routing. Use for 2-week observational period on canary traffic.
Add API to let customers opt into 'auto-substitute-on-deprecation' with two flavors: 'best-effort' and 'strict-similarity' (similarity uses eval-based score thresholds).
Ensure compatibility checks query model manifest metadata (schema fingerprint, function signatures) rather than relying on model name only.
config_schema_example:
policy_name: compatibility_sentinel
version: 1
priority_strategy: latency_preference  # options: latency_preference | cost_preference | strict_compat
steps:
  - type: same_region_variant
    allowed_quantization: [int8, fp16]
    max_latency_increase_ms: 25
  - type: regional_variant
    prefer_zones: [us-west-2, us-east-1]
    max_latency_increase_ms: 50
  - type: cross_region_redirect
    require_auth: false
    max_latency_increase_ms: 150
  - type: hold_and_queue
    timeout_ms: 5000
  - type: fail_with_explanation
    message: 'Pinned version unavailable. See audit log for substitution path.'
test_plan: Unit tests for policy parser and decision tree (mocked candidate lists).
Integration test in staging with pinned route and simulated regional outage; verify ordered substitutions and generated audit entries.
Semantic-regression tests: for auto-substitute-on-deprecation ensure eval score delta <= configurable threshold across a representative prompt set.
Chaos test: throttled KV cache and cold-start spike to exercise 'hold_and_queue' path; assert graceful degradation and bounded error rate.
Security test: verify audit log entries are tamper-evident and KMS signatures are present when security_review_required is true.
rollout_plan: Step 1 (Week 1): Merge policy schema and basic runtime hooks behind feature flag 'compat-sentinel' on staging. Dry-run enabled; emit events but do not route.
Step 2 (Week 2): Enable dry-run on 10% of production read traffic for non-sensitive customers; collect similarity and latency delta metrics.
Step 3 (Week 3): Allow controlled auto-substitute for internal customers only with 'best-effort' strategy; monitor rollback rate <1%.
Step 4 (Week 4): Open to selected customers (opt-in) and run a 2-week canary with strict alerting on semantic regressions and increased error budget consumption.
Step 5 (Week 6): Full rollout if canary success metrics met; otherwise iterate on policy thresholds and compatibility checks.
Rollback criteria: any increase in semantic-regression alerts above threshold, or sustained latency P95 increase >25% on pinned routes for 10 minutes.
monitoring: Per-pin substitution_rate (per-minute) tagged by reason enum.
Per-pin semantic_regression_rate derived from eval-set comparisons.
Latency deltas (P50/P95) before and after substitution for pinned requests.
Audit log completeness gauge and KMS-signature verification count.
Alert: substitution_rate > 0.5% AND customer_impact = high triggers PagerDuty to platform-resilience.
